title: End-Permian terrestrial turnover in the Karoo Basin
summary: In South Africa's Karoo Basin, high-precision uranium-lead dating of volcanic ash at Farm Nooitgedacht established an age of 252.24 ± 0.11 million years for the lower Lystrosaurus Assemblage Zone. This demonstrated that the classic terrestrial vertebrate turnover from Daptocephalus to Lystrosaurus preceded the global marine extinction crisis at Meishan by over 300,000 years, overturning decades of assumptions that terrestrial and marine ecosystem collapses were globally synchronous.

uncertainty.note: 2-sigma analytical uncertainty on CA-ID-TIMS U-Pb zircon age from ash-fall deposit in lower Lystrosaurus Assemblage Zone at Farm Nooitgedacht 68 (Gastaldo et al. 2020).

importance.justification: High-precision radioisotopic dating decoupled the vertebrate faunal turnover in the Karoo Basin from the marine extinction at Meishan, proving that Southern Hemisphere terrestrial ecosystem collapse was not synchronous with the marine crisis.
